troponin.short: A three-part protein complex on the thin filament. When Ca²⁺ binds its troponin C part, it pulls tropomyosin aside so myosin can bind actin.

tropomyosin.short: A long protein strand lying along the actin filament. At rest it blocks myosin's binding sites; troponin moves it when Ca²⁺ arrives.

power-stroke.short: The tilt of a bound myosin head that pulls the actin filament 5–10 nm towards the middle of the sarcomere. The force-making step of the cross-bridge cycle.

rigor.short: Myosin bound tightly to actin with no ATP on the head. Only a new ATP can release it; with no ATP at all, as after death, muscles lock stiff (rigor mortis).

myosin-heavy-chain.short: The large motor part of myosin. Its isoform (MHC I, IIa or IIx in human limb muscle) sets how fast a fibre contracts and names the fibre type.

type-i-fibre.short: A fibre with MHC I: slow, low power, rich in mitochondria and capillaries, highly fatigue resistant. Common in endurance athletes' leg muscles.

type-iia-fibre.short: A fast fibre with MHC IIa: quicker and more powerful than type I, still fairly oxidative, but less fatigue resistant.

type-iix-fibre.short: The fastest, most powerful human fibre, with MHC IIx (once called IIb in humans). Few mitochondria; tires quickly. Rare in trained muscle.

hybrid-fibre.short: A fibre that makes more than one MHC isoform at once (I/IIa, IIa/IIx, I/IIa/IIx). Common in fibres that are changing type.

muscle-biopsy.short: A small sample of muscle (tens of mg) taken with a needle, usually from the vastus lateralis, for fibre typing, enzymes or metabolites.

sds-page.short: A lab method that separates proteins by size in a gel. Run on muscle, it shows how much of each MHC isoform is present, in a whole sample or in single fibres.

length-tension.short: How a fibre's isometric force depends on its sarcomere length: highest where actin and myosin overlap best, lower when the sarcomere is stretched or squashed.

force-velocity.short: The faster a muscle shortens, the less force it can make; when it is stretched while active (eccentric), it can make more than its isometric force.

eccentric.short: An active muscle that lengthens while it pulls, such as the quadriceps braking in downhill running. Concentric: shortening. Isometric: no length change.

cadence.short: Pedal revolutions per minute (rpm) in cycling, or steps per minute in running.

torque.short: The turning effect of a force about an axis: force × lever length, in N·m. In cycling, the force on the pedal times crank length.

citrate-synthase.short: The enzyme of the first step of the Krebs cycle. Its activity in a biopsy is one of the most used markers of mitochondrial content.

capillary-density.short: Capillaries per mm² of muscle cross-section, often given also as capillaries per fibre. More capillaries: more surface for oxygen to leave the blood.

a-vo2-difference.short: Arterial minus venous O₂ content: how much oxygen each litre of blood gives up as it passes through. Muscle VO₂ = blood flow × a-vO₂ difference (Fick principle).

detraining.short: The partial or complete loss of training adaptations when training stops or falls too low.

cross-bridge.short: The link a myosin head makes with actin. Each attach–pull–detach cycle splits one ATP and moves the filaments a few nanometres.

sarcomere.short: The repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, about 2 μm long, from one Z-disc to the next. It shortens when actin filaments slide past myosin filaments.

actin.short: The protein of the thin filaments in a sarcomere, anchored at the Z-discs. Myosin heads grab it and pull it towards the middle of the sarcomere.

myosin.short: The motor protein of the thick filaments in the middle of a sarcomere. Its heads bind actin and pull, splitting ATP each cycle.

mitochondria.short: The structures in the cell where the Krebs cycle, beta-oxidation and the electron transport chain run, using oxygen to make most of the ATP.

capillary.short: The smallest blood vessel, between arterioles and venules. Its wall is so thin that gases, nutrients and wastes are exchanged across it.

motor-unit.short: One motor neuron plus all the muscle fibres it supplies. When the neuron fires, all its fibres contract.

ec-coupling.short: The chain from a muscle action potential to contraction: T-tubules, voltage sensors, calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, calcium binding to troponin.

sarcoplasmic-reticulum.short: A network of membrane sacs wrapped around the contractile filaments of a muscle fibre. It stores Ca²⁺, releases it to start contraction and pumps it back (using ATP) to relax.

percentage-point.short: The plain difference between two percentages: 20% to 22% is +2 percentage points, which is a 10% relative rise.

gross-efficiency.short: Mechanical power ÷ metabolic power. In cycling about 20%: the rest of the energy becomes heat.

krebs-cycle.short: A loop of reactions in the mitochondria that breaks acetyl-CoA down to CO₂ and loads NAD⁺ and FAD with electrons.

vo2max.short: The highest rate at which the body can take up and use oxygen, in L·min⁻¹ (absolute) or mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹ (per kg of body mass).

atp.short: The molecule whose splitting (hydrolysis) to ADP and phosphate powers muscle contraction and ion pumps. The only energy currency muscle spends directly.
